title: Evaluation and Characterization of Potential Biomarkers and Molecular Mechanisms of Cardiovascular Disease in Patients With Ullrich-Turner-Syndrom
summary:
Background
Ullrich–Turner syndrome is a congenital change in genetic material affecting girls and women. Health effects vary widely. Changes involving the heart and blood vessels, as well as aspects of physical development and the body’s own chemical messengers, are particularly important. It is not yet well understood which factors explain why some affected women have a substantially higher risk of heart and blood vessel disease than others.

Research question
The aim is to describe women with Ullrich–Turner syndrome in a systematic way and to examine relationships between
- symptoms and quality of life,
- prior health conditions and developmental features,
- findings from the heart ultrasound examination, and
- laboratory measurements obtained from blood samples.
We seek signals that may indicate increased cardiovascular risk and may support earlier and more targeted prevention and follow-up in the future.

Methods
We conduct a registry as a structured collection of data. Participation consists of a single study visit including
- a standardized questionnaire covering prior illnesses, physical development,  everyday symptoms, and quality of life,
- an ultrasound examination of the heart and
- a blood draw.
Blood samples will be stored securely for research purposes and later analyzed using modern laboratory methods to identify biological signals related to disease mechanisms and risk.

interventions.name: Patients with Ullrich–Turner syndrome will undergo a one-time assessment including the “Turner-CVD” questionnaire on medical history, hormonal status, and quality of life, transthoracic echocardiography, and a blood draw with storage of samples in a biobank.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Confirmed diagnosis of Turner syndrome
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Pregnancy
- Intellectual impairment preventing participation in the registry
